claims.text: A machine-learning approach using high-dimensional descriptors of local chemical disorder and force-constant fluctuations will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than averaged-property models.
The target materials are single-phase HEAs synthesized as random solid solutions with significant atomic-scale compositional disorder.
Ab initio-derived and experimental descriptors of force constants and atomic mass, size, and electronegativity variation can be used to screen HEA compositions.
The approach is applicable from ambient to moderate temperatures typical of thermal-insulation applications.
The approach is intended for alloys with marked differences in constituent atomic properties and minimal extrinsic defects.
Local chemical disorder produces atomic-scale force-constant fluctuations in HEAs.
Variation in atomic properties enhances phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces phonon lifetimes.
Enhanced phonon scattering lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Quantifying local disorder will make thermal-property forecasts more reliable.
The model will select HEAs having exceptionally low lattice thermal conductivity.
The model will improve prediction accuracy by approximately 10–30% relative to conventional averaged-property models.
Callaway-Debye or binary-inspired models based on coarse compositional averages do not fully capture local atomic-scale disorder effects.
The approach will be most effective for HEAs with pronounced atomic-size, mass, or electronegativity differences.
Predictive accuracy will diminish when elemental variations are subtle or when phase segregation and extrinsic defects predominate.
The magnitude of the accuracy improvement may vary with HEA system and measurement conditions.
Disorder descriptors should correlate significantly with measured phonon-scattering behavior.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 10–30% improvement in prediction accuracy, whereas the falsification rule tests for a 10–20% reduction in measured thermal conductivity relative to conventional predictions. Prediction accuracy and conductivity reduction are different quantities, so the benchmark does not directly test the stated performance claim.
